Frugal innovation through internet of things (IoT)
Internet of Things, or IoT, is a network of physical devices. These devices can transfer data to one another without human intervention.
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0040162524000829

IoT refers to a network of physical devices, vehicles, appliances, and other physical objects that are embedded with sensors, software, and network connectivity, allowing them to collect and share data.
IoT = sensing + processing + communication/data exchange.
Some examples…
Smart agriculture
Soil-moisture sensor → microcontroller → internet → farmer's phone.
The farmer receives an alert when the soil becomes dry.
Smart electricity meter
A meter measures electricity consumption and sends data automatically to the utility company.
Smart home
A temperature sensor detects room temperature and communicates with a smart AC to adjust cooling.
Remote patient monitoring
Sensors measure heart rate, SpO₂, temperature → data transmitted to a mobile/cloud platform → doctor can monitor patient remotely.
Smart water tank
A water-level sensor detects the tank level and sends an alert when the tank is nearly empty or full.
Predictive maintenance
Vibration and temperature sensors monitor a motor → abnormal readings are transmitted → maintenance is performed before the motor fails.
Smart waste management
A sensor detects how full a garbage bin is → sends information to the municipal system → collection is scheduled only when needed.
Building Blocks of Frugal IoT
Example: Water Tank Monitoring
Normal IoT:
Industrial water-level sensor → Wi-Fi/4G → Cloud → App
Frugal IoT:
Ultrasonic sensor → ESP32 → local decision → SMS/alert
Frugal idea: Don't continuously send water-level data. Send an alert only when the tank is empty, full, or abnormal.

Note: This approach can also be applied to a general IoT system. However, a frugal IoT system should be specifically designed according to the application requirements, available resources, and cost constraints.
Normal Vs Frugal IoT
| Normal IoT | Frugal IoT
Objective | Maximum functionality and performance | Essential functionality at minimum cost
Cost | Can be relatively high | Affordable
Sensors | Multiple high-end sensors | Only essential sensors
Processing | Cloud/edge processing may be sophisticated | Simple local processing where possible
Connectivity | Wi-Fi/5G/high-bandwidth networks | Low-cost options such as BLE, LoRa, 2G/4G, etc.
Power | May require continuous power | Designed for low power/battery operation
Data | Large amounts of data | Only necessary data
Maintenance | May require specialized support | Easy to repair and maintain locally
Target users | General/industrial/high-end markets | Resource-constrained or underserved users
Design philosophy | "What more can we add?" | "What is the minimum we need?"
Why Frugal IoT Matters
Not every IoT solution needs expensive sensors, cloud computing, or high-end hardware. Frugal IoT aims to deliver maximum value with minimum resources.

Case study
Small and medium-sized apartment companies want to introduce IoT, but they have several constraints:
Limited budget
Few technical staff
Existing/old infrastructure
High cost of conventional IoT systems
Complex installation and maintenance
So, a conventional smart-apartment solution may be too expensive and complicated for them.
Can we provide basic IoT functions using cheaper, simpler, lower-power technologies?
Integration and Cost Optimization of Lightweight IoT Technology in the Renovation of Small and Medium-Sized Apartments
A conventional IOT system might install expensive smart locks, energy meters, gateways, cloud servers, communication modules, central management systems.

Lightweight IoT technology is a specialized solution engineered for resource-constrained environments. By optimizing hardware design, simplifying communication protocols, and leveraging edge computing, it significantly reduces system power consumption, cost, and complexity while maintaining highly efficient data transmission and processing capabilities.
Objective is not to maximize features, but to provide the necessary functionality at an affordable cost.
Frugal Strategy

Use existing infrastructure: They do not completely replace the apartment's existing locking system. The smart locks are selected so they can work with the existing system. This avoids unnecessary replacement costs.

Use lightweight communication: Instead of expensive/high-power communication systems, they use LoRa/NB-IoT. LoRa is particularly attractive because it provides long-range communication with relatively low power consumption.

They use edge computing rather than sending everything continuously to cloud. Sensor → Local/Edge processing → Useful information → Management system. This can reduce communication, latency, and cloud dependence.
Use open-source software: They use OpenHAB and perform secondary development instead of purchasing an expensive commercial IoT platform.
Reduce maintenance cost: Remote monitoring and diagnosis allow technicians to solve some problems without physically visiting every apartment.
Low-cost sensors are installed in the apartments.

Instead of replacing all the sensors, use adapter software. Different sensors → Adapter → Common data format → Existing management system. So, the apartment can reuse existing infrastructure instead of replacing everything.
Outcome
Operational risks: Sensor failure, Communication interruption, Data security

Distinguishing Frugality from Efficiency in AI
Efficiency focuses on optimizing performance metrics (such as speed, accuracy, and energy usage) within a given framework. The goal is to maximize output for any fixed level of resource input.
Frugality starts with the assumption that resources are scarce and seeks to develop solutions that are inherently low-cost and sustainable.
Efficiency improvements are often applied as optimizations to existing systems, such as refining algorithms or reducing computational overhead.

Frugal innovation involves rethinking the system from ground up, incorporating resource constraints into design process itself. This can lead to entirely new approaches that differ from traditional methods.

Case study: Frugal Internet of Things From Artificial Neural Network to Predict Student Mindfulness Concentration and Relaxation Levels
Indoor environmental quality significantly impacts student learning performance and efficiency. Studies indicate that indoor lighting highly affects student learning performance.
Warm color temperature (1000 K) is beneficial to learner's meditation, while a cold color temperature (7000 K) effectively enhances mindful attention.
In indoor environments, subjects better concentrated on with a higher CCT (Correlated Color Temperature) within a range of CCTs from 2700 to 5700 K.
A frugal Internet of Things (IoT) system to monitor student mindfulness concentration and relaxation levels at different CCTs.

Developed an Internet of Things (IoT) system, which consists of a DHT11 sensor for measuring indoor temperature, a WS2812B sensor for controlling indoor light, a TGAM (ThinkGear ASIC Module) module for measuring EEG, and a GSR (Galvanic Skin Response) sensor for detecting emotions.
**CCT measures color appearance of light
Developing Frugal Internet of Things From Artificial Neural Network to Predict Student Mindfulness Concentration and Relaxation Levels
A frugal ANN-based system was developed to find relationships between CCT and student attention and meditation based on EEG and GSR data
Attention (ATT) and Meditation (MED) measured by TGAM
They tested students under two CCT conditions:
Warm light: 2700 K
Cooler light: 5300 K
They found that cool CCT produced higher attention during the English typing tests.
What is the need?
Monitor student concentration and relaxation under different lighting.
What is the conventional expensive solution?
Sophisticated EEG/physiological monitoring and dedicated laboratory equipment.
What did they do instead?
Combine low-cost sensors, microcontrollers, and ANN.
Frugal AI Methods

Model Compression
Pruning: Remove unnecessary connections/weights from the model.
Knowledge Distillation: A large teacher model teaches a smaller student model.
Quantization: Use fewer bits, like 32-bit to 8-bit, to reduce memory and computation.
Frugal and Optimized Algorithms
Adaptive Model Utilization: Use different model sizes depending on the situation.
Zero Time Waste: Avoid unnecessary computation or processing.
Prototype-based Methods: Compare new data with representative examples instead of processing everything.
Data-Efficient Algorithms: Learn effectively using less training data.
Feature Selection
Filter Methods: Select features using simple statistical measures.
Wrapper Methods: Test different feature combinations and choose the best.
Embedded Methods: Feature selection happens during model training.
Hybrid Methods: Combine two or more selection methods.
Ensemble Feature Selection: Use several methods/models together to select important features.
Data Sampling
Undersampling: Reduce the number of training samples.
Data Selection: Select only the most useful samples.
Dataset Distillation: Create a very small dataset that retains the important information of a large dataset.
Hyperparameter Optimization
Neural Architecture Search: Automatically find a suitable neural-network structure.
Inverse Modeling: Work backward from desired performance to find suitable model settings.
Hardware-based methods
ML Accelerators: Special hardware designed specifically for AI operations.
Neuromorphic Hardware: Hardware inspired by brain using neurons/spikes.
Approximate Memory Architectures: Allow small computation/memory errors to save energy.
Model Adaptation: Change the model according to the available hardware resources.

Challenges of Frugal AI
Lack of Data: Frugal AI often has to work in places where good-quality data is limited.

Frugal AI often needs to run on low-cost and resource-constrained devices, such as: Smartphones, Microcontrollers, Edge devices, Low-cost FPGA/embedded systems. These devices may have limited: CPU + Memory + Storage + Battery. So, a large AI model that works well on a GPU may not work on a small embedded device.

Evaluation Metrics and Benchmarks: A major issue is that conventional AI evaluation usually focuses heavily on accuracy. But for Frugal AI, accuracy alone is not enough. You should also ask: How much memory does it require? How much energy does it consume? How much does the hardware cost? How fast does it run? How much data is required? Can it run offline? Is it fair and private?
Security and Privacy: Frugal AI frequently uses edge devices and distributed devices, creating security and privacy challenges.
Ethical and Social Implications: Even if Frugal AI is cheap and efficient, is it safe and fair for society?

Hotels and hospitality companies are increasingly adopting IoT, AI, cloud computing, digital platforms, automation, data analytics.
These technologies can improve guest experience, operational efficiency, resource management, personalization, decision-making.
However, small and medium-sized hospitality businesses often cannot afford expensive AI infrastructure.
They may not have large computing systems, large datasets, highly skilled AI personnel, large technology budgets, sophisticated digital infrastructure.
Can hospitality organizations achieve smart services using AI with limited resources

Frugal Machine learning (FML)
FML aims to make AI more accessible and sustainable, particularly in resource constrained environments such as smart environments, IoT systems, and embedded platforms.

FML emphasizes reducing costs associated with data, computation, and time while maintaining model performance across various ML tasks. TinyML is designed for ultralow-power devices like micro-controllers and edge devices, optimizing models for minimal memory, processing power, and energy consumption. FML is broader and cost driven, while TinyML is specialized for small, resource-limited hardware platforms.
Case study: Frugal Object Detection Models
Object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves both identifying objects and determining their precise locations within images or video frames.
Frugal Object Detection Models: Solutions, Challenges and Future Directions
Traditional object detection relied on hand-crafted features combined with classical machine learning classifiers.
With the advent of deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) revolutionized object detection by enabling end-to-end feature extraction and classification.
Standard Datasets for Object Detection database: 1) COCO Dataset, 2) PASCAL VOC Dataset, 3) Tiny-ImageNet and Custom Edge AI Datasets
CNN-Based Lightweight Models remain a dominant approach for object detection, with various lightweight models optimized for frugality.
YOLOv5-Nano: A compact version of YOLOv5 designed for edge computing with reduced parameters and FLOPs
YOLOv8-Nano: Further improvements in detection speed and accuracy while maintaining a low computational footprint.
LeYOLO: Lightweight-energy variant of YOLO designed for embedded AI applications
Trade-Offs Between Model Complexity and Performance
Frugal object detection requires balancing model complexity with detection accuracy.
Model Size vs. Accuracy: Reducing parameters improves efficiency but may degrade performance.
Inference Speed vs. Computational Cost: Lightweight models run faster but may sacrifice precision in object localization.
Feature Extraction Depth: Shallow networks require less computation but may struggle with detecting small or overlapping objects.
Comparison of Hardware-Specific Optimizations for Frugal Object Detection

Certain hardware platforms are designed to efficiently run lightweight object detection models. These platforms provide dedicated AI acceleration, optimizing real-time processing for edge applications.
